body: Rule 1 - good companies: high ROCE in cash terms, high gross margins (pricing power), high cash conversion, low leverage, growth that can be reinvested, resilience to obsolescence; avoid banks, heavy cyclicals, airlines, conglomerates. Rule 2 - don't overpay: compare free-cash-flow yield with bond yields and the company's growth. Rule 3 - do nothing: minimise turnover and trading costs; let compounding work. Measured over 2010-2025 the approach beat MSCI World (13.8% vs 12.1% a year) but lagged five calendar years in a row (2021-25), when mega-cap tech concentration, passive flows and de-rating of 'quality defensives' hurt. Indian application: the checklist is close to the Marcellus/consistent-compounder template; the binding constraint in India is rule 2 - quality FMCG/consumer names at 60-80x earnings can deliver low single-digit returns for years even as earnings grow.
title: Terry Smith: buy good companies, don't overpay, do nothing
